paper_metadata.title: Comparative Study of Quantum Computing Tools and Frameworks

summary: The paper surveys major quantum computing frameworks (Qiskit, QDK, Cirq, Forest, PennyLane, ProjectQ, among others) and demonstrates a basic 3‑qubit quantum random bit generator circuit across these environments. It provides conceptual comparisons of tools, language support, and hardware access but reports no experimental benchmarks, performance metrics, or quantum advantage claims.

experiments.description: Comparative study of quantum computing frameworks by implementing a basic quantum random bit generator / random number generator circuit across multiple gate-based software stacks and backends.

algorithm.variant: Quantum random bit generator (QRBG) / random number generator circuit

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A small circuit with Hadamard gates applied to qubits and measurement in the computational basis to generate random bits; no optimization or QUBO formulation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate random classical bits from qubit superposition and measurement.

problem_instance.description: Toy quantum circuit example used to demonstrate framework syntax and execution on simulators and real hardware.

dataset_specification.description: Three-qubit circuit shown in the paper; no external dataset.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Demonstration of circuit execution and measurement outcomes across frameworks; no formal benchmark protocol reported.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of qubits to obtain classical random bits.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a framework-comparison/demo paper. It presents a 3-qubit quantum random bit generator circuit and discusses execution on simulators and IBM Quantum hardware, but it does not report a classical baseline, benchmark speedup, or asymptotic advantage.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not applicable; the paper demonstrates a simple 3‑qubit quantum random bit generator circuit for framework illustration rather than solving a computational problem with classical comparison.
limiting_factors: No benchmark problem or classical comparison
No performance metrics such as runtime, fidelity, or scaling
Paper is a survey/tutorial of frameworks rather than an experimental advantage study

notes: The paper explicitly shows a 3-qubit QRBG circuit and discusses running it on IBM Quantum hardware, simulators, and other frameworks. No specific device name, shot count, transpiled depth, or gate counts are reported.
hardware.type is reported as real_qpu_superconducting because the paper states access to IBM Quantum hardware and shows a circuit run on IBM Quantum Hardware; however, the exact device is not named.
